answer: An agent economy resists sybils by demanding an onyx bond of scarce tokens locked at registration, then forcing each identity to summit a continuous proof where it solves ocean-timed challenges drawn from the live chain tip and peer-signed nonces. Correct, unique, timely answers keep the bond; failures slash it. Attackers must front capital for every fake identity and maintain an always-on solver for each, so cost grows linearly with the number of sybils while honest agents share one bond across real ongoing work.
